sets.title: Recognize
sets.description: Choose the right aspect for politeness, certainty, and experience, then pick between close pairs
sets.descriptionRussian: Выберите правильный вид для вежливости, определённости и опыта, затем выберите из близких пар

items.prompt: A teacher to students (softer command): _____, пожалуйста. (Sit down, please.)
items.hint: Imperfective imperative = invitation. Perfective imperative = sharp command.
items.explanation: Imperfective imperative Садитесь is an invitation (please, take a seat). Perfective Сядьте! sounds like an order.

items.prompt: Definite promise: Не волнуйся, я обязательно _____. (Don't worry, I will definitely call.)
items.promptEnglish: Don't worry, I will definitely call.
items.explanation: Definite commitment (обязательно) uses perfective future: позвоню. Буду звонить would be vaguer, less certain.

items.prompt: Experience: Ты _____ когда-нибудь в Сибири? (Have you ever been to Siberia?)
items.promptEnglish: Have you ever been to Siberia?
items.explanation: Experience question: Ты был в Сибири? (imperfective past). Побывал would focus on a specific completed visit.

items.prompt: Firm deadline: Я _____ отчёт к пятнице. (I will complete the report by Friday.)
items.promptEnglish: I will have the report done by Friday.
items.hint: A deadline with к + dative signals a definite result.
items.explanation: Deadline (к пятнице) + definite commitment = perfective: напишу. The speaker promises a finished product.

minimalPairs.context: Ты _____ суши? - Да, много раз. (Have you tried sushi?)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Have you tried sushi? - Yes, many times.
minimalPairs.explanation: General experience question: imperfective пробовал (Have you ever tried?). The answer 'many times' confirms this is about experience, not one event.

minimalPairs.context: Ты _____ этот торт? Ну как, вкусно? (Did you try this cake? How is it?)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Did you try this specific cake? How is it?
minimalPairs.explanation: Asking about a specific, completed tasting (this particular cake) uses perfective: попробовал.

minimalPairs.context: Не волнуйся. Я _____ тебе. (Don't worry. I will help you. - definite promise)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Don't worry. I will (definitely) help you.
minimalPairs.explanation: Definite commitment: perfective помогу = 'I will help (for sure).' Imperfective буду помогать would be vague: 'I'll be helping (sometime).'

sets.title: Build & Correct
sets.description: Build sentences with correct aspect, then fix aspectual errors
sets.descriptionRussian: Постройте предложения с правильным видом, затем исправьте ошибки вида

errorCorrection.hint: Когда-нибудь (ever) signals a general experience question = imperfective.
errorCorrection.explanation: General experience (когда-нибудь) requires imperfective: пробовал. Попробовал would ask about a specific completed tasting.

errorCorrection.sentence: Она всегда хорошо подготовилась к урокам.
errorCorrection.hint: Всегда (always) marks a habitual action. Habitual = imperfective.
errorCorrection.explanation: Habitual past (всегда) requires imperfective: готовилась. Perfective подготовилась would describe a single completed preparation.

errorCorrection.sentence: Я обязательно буду помогать тебе завтра.
errorCorrection.hint: Обязательно signals a firm commitment, which requires perfective future.
errorCorrection.explanation: Definite commitment (обязательно) requires perfective: помогу. Imperfective буду помогать sounds vague and uncommitted.

translation.english: Don't worry, I will definitely help.
translation.hint: Не + impf imperative (don't worry), then perfective future for firm promise.

translation.english: Have you ever tried Georgian wine?
translation.hint: General experience question: imperfective past пробовал. Georgian = грузинское.

translation.english: She finished the project in three months.
translation.answer: Она закончила проект за три месяца.
acceptableVariants: Она завершила проект за три месяца.
Она сделала проект за три месяца.
translation.hint: Completed result with time frame (за + acc) = perfective past.
translation.grammarFocus: Completed action with time frame = perfective
